episodes.202696: High-based showers and thunderstorms produce strong to severe wind gusts with the high wind of 69 mph at the I-70 and Pecos in Denver. Tree some tree, tree branches, and fencing were blown down.
episodes.202752: Convection across southern Pennsylvania began to develop in an unstable and moist environment ahead of a shortwave trough traversing the area during the afternoon and evening hours of July 9, 2025. Storms initially were sub-severe due to lower shear parameters and low-level lapse rates; however, increasing shear and lapse rates allowed for damaging wind potential within an environment of 700-900 J/kg of DCAPE. Shear oriented out of the southwest, parallel to surface boundaries, led to an increased risk of flash flooding in an environment that sustained over one inch an hour rainfall rates. Multiple instances of trees and wires being knocked down were reported in Lancaster and York counties during the evening hours. Increased rainfall rates falling over fairly moist soils of York County induced flash flooding, with multiple roadways closed in both counties during the evening hours. Heavy rain also caused a basement to collapse in Dover, with water and mud reported over nearby roadways.
episodes.202753: Scattered thunderstorms developed across portions of Middle Tennessee during the afternoon of July 9, 2025. Weak steering flow meant that these storms were generally slow-moving. This combined with above average atmospheric moisture meant that the stage was set for heavy rain and flooding. One thunderstorm in Lawrence and Wayne counties produced four to six inches of heavy rain which caused flooding in the Loretto, St. Joseph, and Iron City areas.
episodes.202762: A mid level shortwave and surface cold front brough a smattering of strong to severe storms to southern New England in the evening and early overnight hours. This resulted in scattered wind damage reports in northeast CT, northern RI, and central MA. It also resulted in some flash flooding in southeast MA.
episodes.202764: A mid level shortwave and surface cold front brough a smattering of strong to severe storms to southern New England in the evening and early overnight hours. This resulted in scattered wind damage reports in central/northeast CT, northern RI, and central MA. It also resulted in some flash flooding in southeast MA.
episodes.202765: A mid level shortwave and surface cold front brough a smattering of strong to severe storms to southern New England in the evening and early overnight hours. This resulted in scattered wind damage reports in central/northeast CT, northern RI, and central MA. It also resulted in some flash flooding in southeast MA.
episodes.202768: An upper-level disturbance interacting with an outflow boundary triggered scattered showers and thunderstorms in the Illinois River Valley during the morning of July 8th.  This initial band of showers tended to dissipate toward midday: however, as the atmosphere destabilized during peak heating, an uptick in convective development was noted further east along and east of I-55 by late afternoon into the evening.  With ample deep-layer moisture in place as evidenced by precipitable water values of 1.75-2.00, the storms that developed were efficient rain-producers.  In addition, atmospheric steering winds were quite weak...leading to slow storm movement.  The end result was highly variable rainfall amounts...with a few spots picking up over 3 inches in a short amount of time.  One of the hardest hit locations was Bloomington-Normal in McLean County where widespread amounts of 3 to 5 inches caused flash flooding of several area streets.  Further south, a few of the cells produced isolated wind damage across parts of Sangamon and Shelby counties.
episodes.202774: An area of slow moving thunderstorms trained along a residual boundary across northeast Maryland. This resulted in heavy rain and a localized two to four inches of rain over a two hour period.
episodes.202776: An anomalously moist airmass ahead of a frontal boundary sparked numerous showers and thunderstorms across Maryland. Instantaneous rain rates approached five to six inches an hour in the bigger storms. Storm total rainfall of one and a half to four inches resulted in flooding and flash flooding in areas throughout the evening of July 9th.
episodes.202777: An anomalously moist airmass ahead of a frontal boundary sparked numerous showers and thunderstorms across Virginia. Instantaneous rain rates approached five to six inches an hour in the bigger storms. Storm total rainfall of one and a half to four inches resulted in flooding and flash flooding in areas throughout the evening of July 9th.
episodes.202780: An anomalously moist airmass ahead of a frontal boundary sparked numerous showers and thunderstorms across the District of Columbia. Instantaneous rain rates approached five to six inches an hour during the evening, but were transient. Storms still dropped a quick one to two inches in twenty minutes, resulting in flash flooding throughout the District.
episodes.202794: Scattered thunderstorm activity occurred during the afternoon and evening of July 9, with a microburst causing a concentrated area of damage in the Tucker Crossroads community of Cherokee County.
episodes.202912: A cluster of storms would form a line in central and north central South Dakota, generating strong winds before weakening. The storms were responsible for breaking 3  power poles in the city of Mobridge, and completely ripping the roof off of a business shop that had been previously damaged by storms. The peak wind gust along the line was 81 mph measured at the South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet station near Lowry.  Additional, isolated thunderstorms in central South Dakota would go on to produce some large hail, up to the size of tennis-ball near the town of Lyman, and locally strong winds north of Fort Thompson which would snap power poles and roll haybales across a field. ||As the system continued east overnight, locally strong winds would result in sending a car into the ditch north of Henry, while lightning would damage the generator circuits at the Clark water tower.
episodes.203092: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon of July 9th across the Coastal Plains and Brush Country. This activity was due to a combination of factors: some atmospheric energy skirting the edge of a ridge in the Gulf, the arrival of the sea breeze, and abundant moisture in the region. A few of these thunderstorms caused isolated instances of marine wind gusts and flash flooding.
episodes.203093: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon of July 9th across the Coastal Plains and Brush Country. This activity was due to a combination of factors: some atmospheric energy skirting the edge of a ridge in the Gulf, the arrival of the sea breeze, and abundant moisture in the region. A few of these thunderstorms caused isolated instances of marine wind gusts and flash flooding.
episodes.203106: A slow moving severe thunderstorm developed along a stationary front in Dodge County. Large hail, downed tree branches, and flooded streets were reported.
episodes.203353: A low pressure system moved through the Great Lakes region, trailing a cold front through the area. Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of the advancing cold front. Some storms produced gusty winds and heavy rainfall.
episodes.203391: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts over Galveston Bay.
episodes.203588: After a few drier days, a stretch of active weather returned to the area beginning on July 7th. This was due to a cold front slowly approaching from the west while the remnants of a tropical system tracked north through the Carolinas and Virginia. While the bulk of precipitation associated with the tropical system stayed well east of the Appalachian Mountains, scattered showers and thunderstorms sprouted up in the lowlands of southeast Ohio ahead of the encroaching front and as a shortwave trough moved through. The front remained fairly stationary over the Ohio River on the 8th of July, then lifted back to the north as a disturbance moved over the Great Lakes region on the 9th. Warm, humid conditions fostered development of showers and thunderstorms each day, with lulls in activity during the overnight hours.||Total rainfall amounts between the 7th and 9th ranged from one to three inches across parts of southeast Ohio, with a pocket of around four inches that fell in Athens County. Heavy rain occurred rapidly and led to flash flooding on a few roads in Athens County on the 7th and in Meigs County on the 9th. In addition, damaging wind gusts embedded within these showers and storms, particularly on July 7th, resulted in downed trees across Athens and Morgan Counties.
episodes.203589: Active weather returned to West Virginia on July 9th in the midst of a cold front slowly approaching from the west. Additional moisture was ushered into the region from the remnants of a tropical system tracked north through the Carolinas and Virginia. While the bulk of precipitation associated with the tropical system stayed well east of the mountains, scattered showers and thunderstorms sprouted up in the lower elevations ahead of the encroaching cold front. The front remained fairly stationary over the Ohio River on the 8th of July, then lifted back to the north in response to a disturbance moving over the Great Lakes region on the 9th. Warm, humid conditions fostered development of showers and thunderstorms each day, with lulls in activity overnight.||Ahead of this event, one to two inches of rain had already fallen across portions of the area from the previous two days. Showers and storms that occurred on July 9th only exacerbated these moisture-laden soil conditions as additional rainfall amounts ranging between one to two inches, with locally higher pockets of three to four inches, took place. Flooding arose as a result, which impacted roads, yards, and low-lying areas in Calhoun, Fayette, Nicholas, Putnam, and Upshur Counties. A mudslide also blocked part of Route 60 in Kanawha County.||In addition to flooding, a few thunderstorms on the 9th grew strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts across Ritchie, Lewis, and Boone Counties. Local power outages occurred in the midst of these storms due to downed trees and power lines in the area.
episodes.203648: A cold front approaching the Appalachian Mountains combined with a hot and humid air mass to produce scattered severe thunderstorms across southwest Virginia. Damaging wind gusts from these storms blew down several trees and power lines, and lightning from one of these storms struck a house and set it on fire in Buckingham County.
episodes.203649: A cold front approaching the Appalachian Mountains combined with a hot and humid air mass to produce a severe thunderstorm in Rockingham County of northwest North Carolina. Damaging wind gusts from this storm blew down three trees with one falling on to a power line, and lightning from this storm also struck and blew up a transformer.
episodes.203663: A cold front entered the Appalachian Mountains and produced numerous severe thunderstorms across southwest Virginia. Damaging wind gusts from these storms blew down numerous trees and power lines. A few of these trees fell on to two houses in Henry County, another house in Pittsylvania County, and a car in Halifax County.
episodes.203664: A cold front entered the Appalachian Mountains and produced scattered severe thunderstorms across northwest North Carolina. Damaging wind gusts from these storms blew down several trees and broke several power poles.
episodes.203760: A stalling cold front resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms. Localized swaths of damaging wind were observed over northern Virginia and Maryland.
episodes.203761: A stalling cold front resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms. Localized swaths of damaging wind were observed over northern Virginia and Maryland.
episodes.203765: A stalling cold front resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms. Localized swaths of damaging wind were observed over northern Virginia and Maryland.
episodes.203801: A cold front ignited scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. The most intense thunderstorms produced localized swaths of damaging wind gusts, with considerable wind gusts measured in southern Maryland.
episodes.203805: A stalling cold front resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms. Localized swaths of damaging wind were observed over northern Virginia and Maryland.
episodes.203822: Scattered thunderstorms moved across portions of northeast Illinois during the afternoon and evening of July 8th producing heavy rain.  One thunderstorm slowly moved across central Cook County and Chicago in the late evening producing torrential rain and flash flooding.
episodes.203892: An isolated thunderstorm produced minor wind damage in Reece.
episodes.203953: Scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms developed across portions of northern and western Oklahoma on the 8th, on the periphery of a convectively modified surface boundary. Despite modest deep-layer wind fields (contributing to modest wind shear), strong instability and consolidated outflow boundaries led to occasional reports of severe wind gusts and thunderstorm wind damage. Large hail was also reported with briefly organized thunderstorms in Garfield and Kiowa Counties.
episodes.203954: Scattered evening thunderstorms developed across portions of western-north Texas on the 8th. Despite modest deep-layer wind fields (contributing to modest wind shear), strong instability and consolidated outflow boundaries led to occasional reports of severe wind gusts.
episodes.204052: An upper trough moved into the Southeast, acting as the main forcing in a strongly unstable environment with weak deep layer shear and high PWAT's. This forcing led to the development of scattered strong to severe convection that moved slowly due to the weak steering flow. The slow moving nature and efficient rainfall from these storms led to an area of flash flooding in Lancaster County, SC.
episodes.204072: A shortwave trough supported a swath of heavy rain along a PWAT gradient with values as high as 1.9 inches across far southwestern Pennsylvania and northern West Virginia. 500-1000 J/kg of MUCAPE and 20 knots of cloud bearing flow supported thunderstorms producing heavy rain and flash flooding.
episodes.204221: An MCS (which originated in southwestern Oklahoma and northern Texas) moved into the northern Permian Basin during the early morning hours of the 9th. Though the system was weakening as it moved into the Permian Basin, it was able to produce damaging winds in Snyder. Flash flooding and water rescues were also reported in Odessa due to heavy rain associated with the decaying MCS.
episodes.204294: Scattered Thunderstorms initiated around 4 PM from eastern Finney and Gray counties , to Pawnee and Edwards counties, before  propagating into a northwest to southeast oriented axis from around Dighton to near Meade by 7 PM. Numerous large hail reports were received in the 1one to two inch category as well as hail damage to vehicles and homes.
episodes.204363: A discrete storm moved across primarily Kit Carson county during the afternoon. A truck was traveling on I-70 was overturned due winds from the storm. Another round of storms moved into Yuma county during the evening leading to a 58 mph wind gust near Hale and caused damage to an outbuilding 7 ENE Heartstrong.
episodes.204415: An upper level low and high moisture content fueled widespread, slow-moving storms across the local area. More diurnal instability developed along the Atlantic coast sea breezes where a few stronger storms with wet downburst winds developed in the afternoon.
episodes.204416: An upper level low and high moisture content fueled widespread, slow-moving storms across the local area. More diurnal instability developed along the Atlantic coast sea breezes where a few stronger storms with wet downburst winds developed in the afternoon.
episodes.204420: A line of storms developed along an outflow boundary the evening of the 8th from earlier storms in Colorado, resulting in hail up to nickel size in Rawlins county and a 60 mph wind gust in Logan county.
episodes.204433: Warm temperatures and a moist atmosphere within a mid-level monsoon moisture plume led to scattered thunderstorms on the afternoon of the eighth. One of these storms became severe near Childress producing quarter size hail. Another storm in northern Crosby County produced a landspout tornado near a thunderstorm outflow boundary. The landspout remained in open fields and caused no known damage.
episodes.204542: An upper level shortwave combined with an extremely humid atmosphere generated several thunderstorms that produced heavy rainfall yielding a few flash floods along with an isolated severe storm in East Tennessee.
episodes.204673: A weak trough of low pressure over the Ohio and Tennessee valley region was in place, along with very anomalous moisture over the Carolinas. Scattered showers and storms over the Appalachians become widespread as they moved into central North Carolina in the evening and overnight hours. Numerous wind and flash flooding reports were recorded over the region.
episodes.204892: At the surface, a cold front slowly approached from the west, with a pre-frontal trough developing ahead of it. Aloft, the area remained generally on the eastern edge of mid/upper level troughing. While shear was not all that impressive (about 25 kt of 0-6km bulk shear), strong heating aided in MLCAPE values reaching about 2000 j/kg. With lift from the aforementioned features, and likely help from the right entrance region of an upper level jet streak, showers and thunderstorms started to develop. Some storms reached severe criteria and produce damaging wind gusts.
episodes.204949: A very unstable atmosphere developed over central and parts of western North Dakota where dewpoint values climbed into the 70s. A dryline moved into the area with thunderstorms rapidly developing, many becoming severe. Large hail was the primary threat, with reports of golf ball size hail in Wells, Burleigh, and Hettinger Counties. There were a few severe wind reports, with the strongest reported wind gust of 69 mph occurring in Kidder County.
episodes.205323: On July 9th, an upper level low tracked northeast across southwest Idaho aiding in thunderstorm development. With a dry boundary layer, and marginal precipitable water values, outflow winds were the primary hazard with burn scar flooding a secondary hazard.
episodes.205342: On July 9th, an upper level low tracked northeast across eastern Oregon aiding in thunderstorm development. With a dry boundary layer, and marginal precipitable water values, outflow winds were the primary hazard with burn scar flooding a secondary hazard.
episodes.205477: A slow-moving cold front stalled over the area resulting in convection over southern CT and causing some road closures.
episodes.205565: A line of showers and thunderstorms formed for the late morning hours in Southeast Missouri. A cold air funnel was observed east of Bernie. MLCAPE values were over 1000J/kg while wind shear was weak.
episodes.205687: From the July 4th weekend into the early part of the following week, a weak upper trough lingered over North and Central Texas, triggering several days of scattered showers and thunderstorms. A saturated atmosphere combined with slow storm motions resulted in numerous flash flooding events throughout the region, particularly in Central Texas.
episodes.205777: Two rounds of high based thunderstorms produced high wind gusts across Sweetwater County. The maximum wind gusts of 61 mph were reported at the Rock Springs Airport and along Interstate 80 to the east of Wamsutter.
episodes.205792: A slow-moving cold front produced heavy rain and flash flooding across portions of the region. This is the same front that caused flash flooding the day prior.
episodes.205796: A slow-moving cold front produced heavy rain and flash flooding across portions of the region.
episodes.205799: A slow-moving cold front produced heavy rain and flash flooding across portions of the region.
episodes.205838: A lee surface trough was situated across the Mid-Atlantic on July 8. Loosely organized storms developed in the afternoon, persisting into the evening hours. A few storms became strong to severe in central and southeast Virginia with a hot and humid airmass in place.
episodes.205839: A lee surface trough was situated across the Mid-Atlantic on July 8. Scattered storms developed in the afternoon, persisting into the evening hours. A line of storms entered the Maryland Eastern Shore in the evening, producing a corridor of wind damage.
episodes.205851: Scattered thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. A few of the storms produced brief strong-to-damaging wind gusts. Meanwhile, slow-moving storms produced torrential rainfall and flash flooding in the city of Lincolnton.
episodes.205853: Scattered thunderstorms developed over upstate South Carolina throughout the afternoon. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Greenwood County.
episodes.205866: A slowly moving through lingered over Maryland, with showers and thunderstorms developing in the afternoon. A few storms produced damaging wind gusts across portions of the Eastern Shore of Maryland.
episodes.205981: Multiple clusters of severe thunderstorms bowed out and produced pockets of damaging wind gusts across the region. A few isolated thunderstorms earlier in the day produced some large hail.
episodes.206037: Several scattered storms developed and intensified across central and eastern portions of the Panhandles during the evening of July 8th. Relatively strong wind shear and instability allowed storms to become severe and bring hail up to half dollar size and 60mph winds to portions of the eastern combined Panhandles, which resulted in crop damage. Additional storms developed along outflow boundaries as they moved across the central Texas Panhandle. These additional storms produced severe wind and hail.
episodes.206038: Several scattered storms developed and intensified across central and eastern portions of the Panhandles during the evening of July 8th. Relatively strong wind shear and instability allowed storms to become severe and bring hail up to half dollar size and 60mph winds to portions of the eastern combined Panhandles, which resulted in crop damage. Additional storms developed along outflow boundaries as they moved across the central Texas Panhandle. These additional storms produced severe wind and hail.
episodes.206106: Strong thunderstorms moved off the Catalina and Rincon Mountains southwestward into the Tucson Metro area. The strong winds of 45-51 mph caused roof damage on the east side of the metro and lofted up dust reducing visibilities to between 5-6 miles.
episodes.206120: Numerous thunderstorms developed in the afternoon hours across southeast South Carolina. These thunderstorms produced frequent cloud to ground lightning, with one strike causing significant damage to a home in Colleton County.
episodes.206121: Numerous thunderstorm clusters developed inland across portions of southeast Georgia and southeast South Carolina in the afternoon hours. These storms progressed to the coast and spread out across the Atlantic coastal waters into the evening producing strong wind gusts.
episodes.206130: Remnant tropical moisture along with an upper level area of low pressure resulted in showers and thunderstorms across portions of the northwest Hill Country, which produced flash flooding on July 7th. Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of the Concho Valley and Big Country on July 8th and July 9th, producing severe wind gusts.
episodes.206170: A lee surface trough was situated across the Mid-Atlantic on July 8. Loosely organized storms developed in the afternoon, persisting into the evening hours. A few storms became strong in central and southeast Virginia with a hot and humid airmass in place, resulting in localized flash flooding.
episodes.206234: A short wave trough aloft approached the Mid-Atlantic from the west on July 9. Strong thunderstorms formed during the afternoon and evening with gusty winds and heavy rainfall.
episodes.206322: A thunderstorm produced a severe wind gust at the Orlando Executive Airport.
episodes.206420: A short wave trough aloft approached the Mid-Atlantic from the west on July 9. Strong thunderstorms formed during the afternoon and evening with gusty winds and heavy rainfall.
episodes.206800: An area of low pressure centered offshore of southern Oregon and far northern California sent mid-level moisture northward and created an unstable air mass, leading to the development of a severe thunderstorm with strong straight line, downdraft winds in the Rogue Valley cities of Central Point, Medford, and Jacksonville.
